subject: Service redistribution notice + customer action checklist (APAC/EU impact)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Acme AI Ops <ops@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Aug 2029 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Service redistribution notice + customer action checklist (APAC/EU impact)

Hi team,

We wanted to let you know we're seeing degraded inference capacity and elevated 502/timeout rates for requests routed through EU and APAC regions starting ~08:50 UTC this morning. The immediate issue is a peering flap impacting control-plane reconcilers in those cloud regions which is causing autoscale thrash for certain Dedicated pools and elevated cold-starts for Hosted customers.

What you need to know (short):
- Impacted regions: eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1 (some hosts reporting > 30% request errors or slow tails).
- User-visible: intermittent 502s and >500ms tail latency for generation endpoints when routed to EU/APAC.
- Current mitigation: automated routing is preferring US regions for new traffic but some customers still receive EU/APAC endpoints depending on DNS/edge affinity.

Action required from Acme (recommended, low-risk):
1) Prefer US endpoints for the next 4-12 hours. You can do this by setting the region hint in your Redwood client: region=us-east-1 or by pinning calls to api.redwood.ai?region=us-east-1.
2) If you control edge DNS, reduce weight for eu and apac pools temporarily (TTL 60s).
3) If you use our SDK, set prefer_low_latency=false to force region-stable routing (example in attachment).

We attached a short step-by-step guide (temporary-redispatch-steps.pdf) and a one-page list of curl examples (api-region-examples.txt). We'll keep this thread updated — next update in ~30 minutes or sooner if anything changes.

Apologies for the disruption. We're treating this as Sev-2 and engineering is working the cloud provider-side peering fix. If you prefer, we can schedule a short call to walk through updates and apply a manual traffic migration.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]

Hi — quick answers and explicit examples below. I'll also paste these to our runbook.

1) curl examples (region hint and DNS TTL guidance):

# Short-lived region hint via query param
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?region=us-east-1" 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha", "input":"Hello"}'

# SDK (python) region hint example
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY", region="us-east-1")
resp = client.generate("Hello")

DNS guidance: set eu and apac region weights to 0.1 (or 0) temporarily; reduce TTL to 60s during the migration window.

2) Cache/session impact:
- Short answer: there is minimal impact for stateless generation calls. For chat/session flows that rely on instance-local KV caches, switching regions may cause cold-cache behavior and slightly higher latency for a few calls while caches warm. We do not delete user data on routing; messages and history are retained in your configured retention. If you need sticky session guarantees, we can provision a temporary Dedicated pool in us-east to preserve cache locality — I can spin that up with approval.

3) SLA and credits:
- We will follow standard SLA policy. I have looped in Marissa (CS lead) to handle formal credit requests and procurement correspondence. Please keep any request details in this thread so we can track.

I'll remain on standby; if you want we can do a 15-minute call to run the migration commands with your infra team.

Jordan

Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — 2029-08-12 regional peering disruption

Hi all,

Thanks again for your patience while we worked through the peering instability. This is a post-incident summary and list of follow-up actions.

What happened (brief):
- Timeline: 08:50 UTC on Aug 12 — 14:00 UTC on Aug 12. Root cause: a tier-1 cloud backbone peering configuration change that caused transient BGP flaps between eu-west-1 and our Dedicated host subnets. That resulted in delayed control-plane reconciliation and autoscaler instability for some Dedicated pools.

Customer impact:
- Intermittent 502s and elevated tail latency for EU/APAC-routed inference calls. Some customers with strict edge affinity saw request routing remain to impacted pools until DNS TTLs expired.

Immediate mitigations we took:
- Automated routing preference applied to favor US regions for new allocations.
- Manual traffic redistribution guidance provided (see Jordan's checklist).
- Short-term capacity increase in us-east to absorb shifted traffic.

Permanent mitigations and action items (owner / ETA):
- Implement control-plane retry window smoothing to reduce autoscaler thrash — Engineering (Grace O'Connor) / 3 weeks.
- Add BGP flapping detection and automated zone-avoidance rule — Networking / 4 weeks.
- Update customer runbooks with explicit region-failover steps and sample SDK flags — DevEx (Jordan Blake) / 1 week.
- SLA/credit review for impacted customers — CS (Marissa Cole) / 2 business days.

SLA/credits: We are reviewing the affected windows and will send a formal credit proposal by EOD tomorrow. Please reply to this thread if you have billing specifics to include.

If you have any remaining concerns or want a walk-through of the failover commands and steps, I can arrange a 30-minute call with our engineering lead.

Apologies again for the disruption — we will follow up once the above mitigations are complete and the credit review is finalized.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
